key_insight: Wall curvature reshapes supersonic turbulence: concave walls promote structured triadic energy transfer and vortex breakdown, while convex walls suppress redistribution and retain energy in elongated streamwise streaks.
engineering_relevance: Distinguishing nonlinear scale selection from linear flow receptivity can inform turbulence modeling and flow-control strategies for curved supersonic surfaces.
method: Direct numerical simulations over concave and convex walls
Scale-resolved TKE budgets, triadic bispectra, and SPOD
Global resolvent analysis of linear amplification
evidence_signal: DNS-based diagnostics identify low-spanwise-wavenumber outer-layer production over concave walls and suppressed pressure-strain redistribution over convex walls, with resolvent analysis linking coherent-structure topology to mean-flow receptivity.
watch_item: Generality beyond the simulated conditions remains unestablished; the abstract reports no experimental validation.
paper_title: Triadic energy cascades and linear amplification mechanisms in supersonic turbulent boundary layers over curved walls
